title: Review Sam's pull request
seo: Power BI code review drill: review a TMDL pull request with calculated columns on a fact table, a bi-directional relationship, duplicate and badly named measures.
summary: Sam's PR adds margin to the shared model. It's due in today's release train. Review the diff and decide: approve, or request changes?
impact: Review is the cheapest place to stop a slow, wrong or confusing change. After it ships, every report built on the shared model inherits the problem.

messages.subject: PR-231: Add margin to the sales model
body: Jordan needs margin by customer for Monday. Adds Line Margin and a few measures. Tested in Desktop, numbers look right. Can you approve before the 3pm train? 🙏

evidence.title: Team modeling standards (excerpt)
body:
- Measures: descriptive names, display folder, description, format string; use DIVIDE.
- No calculated columns on fact tables over 1M rows unless agreed; push logic upstream.
- Relationships single direction unless an ADR says otherwise.
- One measure per concept: no duplicates.

tasks: Review the diff line by line. Write each comment as you would on GitHub: the line, the problem, why it matters, the suggested change.
Decide approve / request changes, and say what must change before the 3pm train and what can follow later.
hints: There are six distinct problems in fifteen added lines: two columns, four measures, one relationship. Check each against the team standards.
For each problem ask: is it wrong, slow, confusing or risky? Wrong and risky block the merge; confusing can sometimes be a follow-up.

rubric.good: All six issues found: calculated column on the fact, text year column, m1 naming and / operator, duplicate margin measures, hard-coded year, bi-directional relationship (plus missing descriptions).
Each comment says why it matters (performance, correctness, maintainability, ambiguity).
Concrete alternatives: margin in the source or as a measure with SUMX, DATESYTD or a year filter on DimDate, single direction.
Respectful, specific; clear decision with what blocks and what can follow.

retro: Which of these would a Best Practice Analyzer rule catch automatically?
How do you review fast without rubber-stamping?
